notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/amountinput.guide.tsx, which registers src/AmountInputGuide.tsx) and docs/evidence/amountinput.md at 31f1c5e (“docs: add onboarding home page, component search, and favicon”, 29 September), the same files on main and docs-next. The guide's Sources note and the evidence were checked on 22 September 2026 on jfs-components 0.1.60, so items citing them carry 2026-09-22 and 0.1.60 and the trace check flags them; the mirror has no 0.1.60 tag, so no GitHub compare to the installed build is possible, and every sentence quoted here was read against the installed source instead. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Builds compared (blob SHAs through gh api): AmountInput.tsx is the same blob (3d7ccc3) at v0.1.78, -636f3f5, -c1fa197, -a116616, -c7d3348 and -dbe0e02. MoneyValue.tsx is 3f81f58 from v0.1.78 to c7d3348 and 7e013fd at dbe0e02; the change is accessibility only (the amount row is now a View with role img, or a Pressable with role button when editable or pressable, named by accessibilityLabel or the currency and amount, lines 330–375 and 434–450), with no change to its tokens, layout or editing. NoteInput.tsx is 49d956d at v0.1.78 and 636f3f5 (state accepted and never read; controlled only) and 09c1ecd from c1fa197 to dbe0e02. The design-tokens JSON is 0582bb0 at v0.1.78 and 4545aec from 636f3f5 to dbe0e02, and every amountInput/*, moneyValue/* and noteInput/* token resolves to the same value on both through the package's own getVariableByName (no modes, Context3 Amount Input, Transaction Bubble and Balance & Cards, Color Mode Dark, Page type SubPage); the resolver (d03e77c) is the same at every tag. Installed source read for each sentence used (read, not rendered; token values through lib/commonjs getVariableByName): AmountInput.tsx takes moneyValueSlot, noteInputSlot, modes and style and nothing else (lines 10–23); it merges the provider's modes with its own (36–37) and clones that set onto each slot element, replacing the child's own modes (54–57, 66–69); an omitted slot falls back to a MoneyValue or a NoteInput with those modes (59–61, 71–73); the container is a centred column with amountInput/gap 16 and padding 0 in every mode, and no width (40–51), the MoneyValue first and the note second (77–82). It sets no Context3 of its own (Balance, RechargeCard and TransactionBubble set theirs; nothing in the package sets Amount Input), so with none the moneyValue tokens are Default: currency and amount 14 px on an 18 px line, weight 500; with Context3 Amount Input the currency is 32 px and the amount 56 px (lines raised to 39 and 68 by safeTextLineHeight), weight 900, the evidence's Figma sizes. MoneyValue.tsx: value defaults to '500' and currency to '₹' (98–99); currency takes a symbol, or an ISO code it maps to a symbol (22–54, 188–195), drawn before the amount in a row (219–223, 384–386); editable defaults to false (103), and with it a tap opens an inline number field that accepts digits and one decimal point and calls onValueChange with the new amount on blur or submit (138–169, 322–328, 390–411); the display always shows the value prop (116–128), so the screen passes a new amount back. NoteInput.tsx: placeholder defaults to “Add note” (45); without value it keeps its own text and still calls onChangeText (55–57, 148–151); its text is 14 px, weight 700 in every mode (76–81, 122–131); maxWidth 100% and flexShrink 1, and a long note wraps (104–105, 110–120). Contradicted by the installed build and left out: the Sources sentence “The NoteInput state prop is accepted but unused by the implementation; its visible editing state is focus-driven.” (state Editing hides the placeholder as focus does: NoteInput.tsx 50, 68–69, 170, 177), and the States description's second sentence, “NoteInput responds to focus and controlled text; its internal state is runtime-driven.”, which says less than the package (a note with no value keeps its own text, 55–57 and 148–151). Both changed between the 8 October (636f3f5) and 12 October (c1fa197) builds; they are the guide fix in reviews/amountinput.json (human flag on the whole entry). Out of date and not used: the Sources “exports from jfs-components 0.1.60” and the evidence's batch line (declared and resolved 0.1.60). Not re-checked and not used: the Figma node and the Storybook story ids the Sources note lists (the Storybook gap keeps its 0.1.60 date). Not recorded: style (the building rules keep style off Coin components); Page type (no guide sentence covers it; JioPlus turns the amount white) and Color Mode (building rules); MoneyValue's hidden, focused, negative and style props, and NoteInput's props other than placeholder, value and onChangeText (they belong to those components; only the playground's “Hide amount for privacy” shows hidden); the playground and its readout; the accessibility labels the guide's code passes (“Edit amount”, “Add note”), which no copy explains; the CSS clip of the Don'ts' teaching frame. Strength: no quote holds must, never, always, only or required. Anatomy: Amount and Note are always present, because an omitted slot falls back to a default MoneyValue or NoteInput, so the Note is optional detail for people, not an optional part; Currency is not, because an empty currency leaves the amount without a unit (the guide's Hide the unit Don't sets currency to an empty string, AmountInputGuide.tsx line 90; MoneyValue.tsx 190). avoidWhen is empty: the guide names no case where another component fits better (slider.json's avoidWhen points typed exact amounts here). accessibility is empty: the guide has no accessibility copy. Content good keeps the guide's notes and placeholders; bad keeps the Don'ts' long note and unbroken value. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every AmountInput, MoneyValue, NoteInput and Card), no modes on the Card (the guide sets AppearanceBrand Neutral) or on the slot children (the guide sets its AMOUNT_MODES on them too, but AmountInput replaces them with its own). Context3 Amount Input is set on AmountInput in each example, as the guide's own source does (AMOUNT_MODES, line 21), because AmountInput doesn't set its own context and passes its modes to both children; without it the amount is 14 px instead of 56 px. MoneyValue has no entry in this pack, but it is the amount slot's own child and the only way to set the amount, as in the NoteInput, Balance, Drawer and List Group entries. The In context example drops the guide's Card style (width 100%). The MoneyValues are editable where the guide's are (In context, Custom slots); the In context note is uncontrolled with onChangeText, the guide's filled notes are controlled, and the literal values and empty handlers stand for the screen's own state. Copy is the guide's own (Review transfer, Enter the amount and an optional note before sending., ₹500, Add transfer note, $1000, Monthly investment, Add investment note, Rent). Left out of examples (three at most): the default slots (the default MoneyValue is a fixed sample ₹500 that can't be edited), Money edit and Note filled (the In context and Custom slots examples show them), the sizing hosts, the Do & Don'ts and the playground. Consistency with earlier entries that use AmountInput: noteinput examples[0] sets Context3 Amount Input on AmountInput only, with a MoneyValue and a NoteInput that carry no modes, which agrees with this entry. The Merchant Profile guide sets Color Mode Light and Context3 Amount Input on AmountInput and on both children (merchantprofile.guide.tsx lines 11 and 76–77); AmountInput's set is the one that reaches them, which agrees; that entry leaves AmountInput out because it had no entry then. slider's avoidWhen sends typed exact amounts to AmountInput or TextInput; that holds when the MoneyValue in moneyValueSlot is editable, as configuration says. Those entries are not changed in this batch. Sorting (batch 13, round 1): the cross-check raised five flags. Four were ours and are fixed: the Default-context rule gave 14 px, which is true on the installed tokens but in neither its fact nor the evidence, so it now says only that the amount and currency render smaller than the Amount Input entry's 56 px and 32 px (the 14 px stays in these notes); the Context3 rule added “Leave Color Mode to the device”, which is a building rule, not the guide's, and is gone; the Currency part was marked always present although the guide's Don't shows an amount without one, so it is now optional; and the Money view example said the view means a non-editable MoneyValue, where an editable one shows the same view until tapped (the guide's Money view card is not editable, AmountInputGuide.tsx line 86 with editable defaulting to false, line 30), so its purpose now says that. The fifth, that the modes rule says a child's modes are replaced, rests on the installed AmountInput.tsx (cloneElement with { modes }, lines 54–57 and 66–69), which the reviewer sees only as rendered copy; its wording is softened to state the behaviour without forbidding modes on children. Round 2 raised three: the Context3 rule dropped the Color Mode=Light the guide's owner passes with it, so it now says that Light is Color Mode's default (the facts' Color Mode default; the 56 px and 32 px come from Context3 alone, the same with and without Color Mode Light through the resolver); the modes rule and the Default-context rule were flagged again and are dismissed in reviews/amountinput.json, because both follow the installed source, which the reviewer doesn't see. Fix loop (release 0.1.78+23, 31 October, for Marcin’s send-back of +16 on Astra’s review): Astra reversed both dismissals. /configuration/4: “passes its context” doesn’t support the added claim that modes set on the slotted MoneyValue or NoteInput are replaced; /configuration/6: modes:Context3 gives the default (Default) and Figma’s Amount Input sizes, not the smaller sizes with Context3 unset. Our misreading in both: the items added behaviour read from the package source that no fact or quote in the entry carries. /configuration/4 now says only what its anatomy sentence says; /configuration/6 says only what modes:Context3 carries (its default is Default, and its evidence description gives Amount Input’s 56 px amount and 32 px currency). The source readings (AmountInput.tsx 54–57 and 66–69 clone each slot child with AmountInput’s modes; 14/14 px through getVariableByName with no Context3 or Default) stay in these notes and in the dismissals’ history, not in rules. Both dismissals are removed from reviews/amountinput.json; the #536 human flag stays.

examples.purpose: A transfer review, the guide's In context: a Card titled for the task gives the entry its context, the AmountInput keeps the amount primary with an editable ₹500 and a note under it, so the person knows what they are completing. AmountInput carries Context3 Amount Input, as the guide's own source sets it, because it doesn't set its own context and passes its modes to both children; the children carry none. The literal amount and the empty onValueChange stand for the screen's own state (MoneyValue shows the value it is given); the note keeps what people type and onChangeText gives the screen each change.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <Card.Title>Review transfer</Card.Title>
  <Card.SupportText>Enter the amount and an optional note before sending.</Card.SupportText>
  <AmountInput
    modes={{ Context3: 'Amount Input' }}
    moneyValueSlot={<MoneyValue value="500" currency="₹" editable onValueChange={(amount) => {}} />}
    noteInputSlot={<NoteInput placeholder="Add transfer note" onChangeText={(note) => {}} />}
  />
</Card>

from.quote: A Card gives the entry a task context while AmountInput keeps amount primary.
